pairs.difference: A (jellyfish): the bell is lacquered all over. It has hard white sparkle dots on the bell, crisp cyan rim lights along the tentacle edges, and glassy bubbles with sharp catchlights. Every part, bell, frills and tentacles, has the same wet sheen, with no matte areas. B (hoop): the backboard is a flat, soft white and the red frame is a smooth, quiet, slightly matte band. The orange rim has one soft highlight and the net is plain rope with no fibre detail. B's surfaces are simple and slightly soft-focus, like the real lesson cards. Its high highlight_share comes from the white board, not from specular hits.
pairs.fix: Make the jellyfish bell soft and milky, like frosted jelly, with one broad, soft highlight on top. No sparkle dots, no glitter specks and no bright rim lights on the tentacle edges. Make the tentacles matte and slightly translucent, and use fewer, softer bubbles.

pairs.difference: A (street lamp): the metal is smooth dark green with soft broad highlights on the cap and ring mouldings. The glass is evenly frosted and the scroll arm is simple and rounded. It has no added micro detail and a slightly soft focus, matching the real cards. B (seahorse): the skin looks hand-painted. Crisp dark spots are stamped over the body, there are many tight ridge lines, and faint mottled noise shows in the orange-to-yellow shading. The fins have sharp painted ribs. Its detail is more decorative and grainier than the smooth real renders. The evidence is weak, because both cards stay within the real ranges.
pairs.fix: Make the seahorse a smooth, soft clay-like toy body. Draw a few broad, rounded ridge bands instead of many thin lines, and fewer, softer, larger spots. Keep the shading clean and smooth with no painted mottling, and use simple fins with two or three soft folds.

pairs.difference: A (campfire): the logs carry lengthwise grain grooves and the cut ends show drawn growth rings, so the wood grain is big and decorative. The stones are speckled, the ground is sprinkled with scattered pebbles, and the background cabin logs repeat the same end-ring motif. Everything is the same satin finish, and A has low gloss_share at 0.024, below the real range. B (binocular viewer): the metal is built from a few broad, smooth parts, with wide collars, a plain coin box and a rounded handle. Its brushed-metal highlights are broad and soft, like the real camera lesson's simplified hardware.
pairs.fix: Draw the logs as smooth, rounded wooden cylinders with only faint, quiet grain and plain, lightly shaded cut ends with no ring pattern. Make the stones smooth and matte with no speckles, remove the scattered pebbles, and give the coffee pot one soft enamel highlight so it reads glossier than the wood.

pattern: Generated cards add fine detail that real cards smooth away: drawn stitch lines and dashed seams, wood grain and ring marks, vent slots, knurled dials, stamped spots, glitter specks. Their highlights are crisp and their edges sharply in focus, often with the same lacquer on every material. Real cards keep a few broad, soft, rounded parts and quiet surfaces. Their gloss is soft and their focus slightly soft.
